before: According to statistics, twice as many people came here as tourists this year as last year.
after: According to statistics, the number of visitors here this year is double last year's.
why: English was clumsy ("twice as many people came here as tourists this year as last year").

before: 请把这份文件传给后面的同学。
after: 请把这些试卷传给后面的同学。
why: "文件传给后面的同学" is an odd pairing; passing test papers back to classmates is the natural classroom scene.

before: Please pass this document to the classmate behind you.
after: Please pass these test papers back to the classmates behind you.

before: 传说这座山洞里藏着很多宝，可是谁也没找到过。
after: 这孩子是全家人的宝，大家都特别疼他。
why: "山洞里藏着很多宝" is unnatural; bare 宝 is not used as a countable "treasure" with 很多 (would be 宝藏/宝贝). "是……的宝" is the idiomatic standalone use.

before: Legend has it that a lot of treasure is hidden in this cave, but no one has ever found it.
after: This child is the whole family's treasure; everyone dotes on him.

before: 他把绳子的两头结在一起，做成了一个圈。
after: 一只蜘蛛在窗户角上结了一张网。
why: "把绳子的两头结在一起" is stilted (natural speech uses 系/打结); 结网 is the idiomatic verb use of 结.

before: He tied the two ends of the rope together to make a loop.
after: A spider has spun a web in the corner of the window.

before: With five minutes left in the match, the players were all running for their lives.
after: With five minutes left in the match, the players were all running as hard as they could.
why: 拼命地跑 means running all-out, not "running for their lives".

before: A crowd gathered at the roadside, watching something.
after: A crowd had gathered at the roadside; I couldn't tell what they were looking at.
why: Translation dropped 不知道在看什么 ("no idea what they were looking at").

before: 警方正在收集证据，准备起诉那个人。
after: 警方正在收集证据，争取早日破案。
why: Police do not 起诉 (prosecutors do); factually wrong collocation.

before: The police are gathering evidence in preparation for charging that man.
after: The police are gathering evidence, hoping to crack the case soon.

before: 这家公司的员工已经从十人增到了一百多人。
after: 这两年，这个城市的人口猛增，房子越来越难租了。
why: "从十人增到了一百多人" mixes bookish 增 with colloquial 到了; standalone 增 is natural in compounds like 猛增.

before: This company's staff has grown from ten to more than a hundred.
after: The city's population has surged in the past two years, and flats are getting harder and harder to rent.

why: "kuno sekali" was a redundant intensified duplicate of "kuno", and "lama" just means "old/long".

before: 他把书在书架上放得很整齐。
after: 他把书架上的书摆得很整齐。
why: "把书在书架上放得很整齐" has awkward word order; 把书架上的书摆得很整齐 is the natural phrasing.

before: He arranged the books very neatly on the shelf.
after: He arranged the books on the shelf very neatly.
